claim: Membrane contact sites enable the efficient transfer of biomolecules between cellular compartments.
source: Actively maintained close appositions between organelle membranes, also known as contact sites, enable the efficient transfer of biomolecules between cellular compartments.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about contact site function.

claim: Contact sites are formed between most, if not all, cellular membranes.
source: Contact sites are formed between most, if not all, cellular membranes (Kakimoto et al., 2018; Shai et al., 2018; Valm et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: Contact sites harbor a defined membrane composition enriched with specific lipids and proteins.
source: To perform these functions, contact sites harbor a defined membrane composition, enriched with specific lipids and proteins, some of which can form tethers between the opposing membranes, enabling a functional interaction (Scorrano et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: The formation and function of the majority of contact sites remains poorly understood.
source: While several contact sites have been observed for decades and we know of multiple tethers and functions for the few well-studied contacts, the formation and function of the majority of contact sites remains poorly understood.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Split fluorescence proteins can be used to visualize contact sites when organelles come into extremely close proximity.
source: In short, each part of a split-Venus protein is used to tag membrane proteins on opposing organelles. Only in instances where these organelles come into extremely close proximity, as is the case at contact sites, the two parts complement each other to form a full fluorophore.
evidence: This describes the technical approach used in the study based on established methodology.

claim: Any membrane protein with the correct topology (terminus facing the cytosol) can be used for the split-Venus assay.
source: Since any membrane protein with the correct topology (terminus facing the cytosol) can be used for this assay (Shai et al., 2018), this approach allows for the visualization of contact sites in the absence of known components.
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: A new reporter for the Golgi-peroxisome (GoPo) contact site was created and characterized.
source: Additionally, we created and characterized a new reporter for the GoPo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental work performed, with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The GoPo contact site is very dynamic, rare, and metabolically regulated.
source: This contact site is very dynamic, rare, and metabolically regulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D), potentially due to the quick turnaround of Golgi cisternae.
evidence: Supported by reference to figure data and includes speculation about mechanism.

claim: The NVJ reporter served as a positive control because it is one of the more characterized contacts.
source: The NVJ reporter served as a positive control, as it is one of the more characterized contacts, therefore in an effective screen we would expect to identify many of its known components.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental design based on existing knowledge.

claim: 1165 strains each expressing one mCherry-tagged protein under the strong TEF2 promoter were screened.
source: To identify potential new contact site proteins, we generated strains expressing each of the above-mentioned reporters and crossed them against a collection of 1165 strains each expressing one mCherry-tagged protein under the strong TEF2 promoter (Figure 1A; Weill et al., 2018; Yofe et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach with citations to the strain collection.

claim: The screened strains were chosen such that each mCherry-tagged protein is either localized to intracellular puncta or has previously been identified as a contact site protein.
source: The strains were chosen such that each mCherry-tagged protein is either localized to intracellular puncta – the typical cellular distribution of contact site proteins – or has previously been identified as a contact site protein (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for the screen.

claim: A total of 158 unique proteins were identified across all six contact sites.
source: A total of 158 unique proteins were identified across all six contact sites (Supplementary file 2, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the screening results with reference to supplementary data.

claim: The NVJ screen identified 20 proteins that co-localize with and/or affect the contact.
source: When looking at our positive control, the NVJ (Figure 1C), we found 20 proteins that co-localize with and/or affect the contact.
evidence: This is a direct statement of screening results with reference to figure.

claim: The validated NVJ residents Nvj1, Nvj3, Mdm1 and Lam6 were identified in the NVJ screen.
source: Among these were the validated NVJ residents Nvj1, Nvj3, Mdm1 and Lam6 (Elbaz-Alon et al., 2015; Henne et al., 2015; Murley et al., 2015; Pan et al., 2000), demonstrating the potential power of our approach.
evidence: This is a statement of screening results validated by citations to published research.

claim: Overexpression of mCherry-Erg2 reduced the frequency and brightness of the NVJ reporter signal.
source: Additionally, overexpression of mCherry-Erg2 reduced the frequency and brightness of the reporter signal, suggesting that modulation of the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway affects the formation of the NVJ.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the screen with interpretation.

claim: Several NVJ resident proteins play a role in sterol sensing and transport, specifically Lam5, Lam6, and Osh1.
source: This is particularly interesting, since several NVJ resident proteins play a role in sterol sensing and transport, specifically Lam5, Lam6, and Osh1 (Gatta et al., 2015; Levine and Munro, 2001; Murley et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: The NVJ has been shown to play a role in the mevalonate pathway by facilitating the assembly of HMG-CoA reductases during acute glucose restriction.
source: and this contact has also been shown to play a role in the mevalonate pathway by facilitating the assembly of HMG-CoA reductases, and consequently affecting activity of these enzymes, during acute glucose restriction (Rogers et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: The pCLIP screen identified 37 proteins that co-localize with and/or affect the contact.
source: One interesting yet uncharacterized contact site in yeast is the pCLIP, between the PM and LDs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), where we identified 37 proteins that co-localize with and/or affect the contact (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of screening results with reference to figures.

claim: Mdm1 was identified in the pCLIP screen.
source: From these we identified Mdm1, a known contact site protein that localizes to a three-way LD-ER-vacuole contact (Hariri et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a screening result supported by citation to published research.

claim: The Drosophila melanogaster homolog of Mdm1, Snazarus, localizes to a triple contact that involves LD-ER-PM membranes.
source: Interestingly, the Drosophila melanogaster homolog of Mdm1, Snazarus, also localizes to a triple contact that instead involves LD-ER-PM membranes (Ugrankar et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: Mdm1 and Snazarus bind LDs via different domains and have different specificity for membrane lipids.
source: Although Mdm1 and Snazarus bind LDs via different domains, and have different specificity for membrane lipids, this new localization for Mdm1 suggests it could also play a role at a yeast LD-ER-PM contact site.
evidence: This is a statement combining known information with speculation about function.

claim: Hob1 (formerly Fmp27), Hob2 (formerly Ypr117w), and Csf1 are remote homologs of AsmA, a bacterial relative of Vps13.
source: We found that these are remote homologs of AsmA, a bacterial relative of Vps13 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a result from bioinformatic analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 share full-length structural homology to Vps13 and Atg2.
source: Advanced modelling indicates that they all share full-length structural homology to Vps13 and Atg2 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), two well described long, tubular lipid transfer proteins (Kumar et al., 2018; Li et al., 2020; Maeda et al., 2019; Osawa et al., 2019; Valverde et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a result from structural modeling with citations to published research on Vps13 and Atg2.

claim: Vps13 has been shown to reside at both the NVJ and the vCLAMP in yeast.
source: In yeast, Vps13 has been shown to reside at both the NVJ and the vCLAMP (Lang et al., 2015; Park et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 are predicted to be long, predominantly hydrophobic, channels that can potentially transport multiple lipid molecules.
source: Like Vps13 and Atg2, these proteins are predicted to be long, predominantly hydrophobic, channels, which can potentially transport multiple lipid molecules (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is based on structural predictions with reference to figures.

claim: C-terminally tagged versions of Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 have been shown to localize to ER-PM and ER-mitochondria contact sites.
source: C-terminally tagged versions of Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 have recently been shown to localize to ER-PM and ER-mitochondria contact sites (Neuman et al., 2022; Toulmay et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: Hob1 and Hob2, and their Drosophila homologue Hobbit, target contact sites through N-terminal transmembrane domains that anchor in the ER and C-terminal elements that bind other organelles including the PM.
source: Hob1 and Hob2, and their Drosophila homologue Hobbit, target contact sites through N-terminal transmembrane domains that anchor in the ER (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B), and C-terminal elements that bind other organelles including the PM (Neuman et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research with reference to figure.

claim: Csf1 has a predicted N-terminal ER anchor.
source: Csf1 also has a predicted N-terminal ER anchor (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B)
evidence: This is based on structural prediction with reference to figure.

claim: Csf1 has been shown to play a role in lipid homeostasis.
source: and has been shown to play a role in lipid homeostasis (John Peter et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: N-terminally tagged Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 co-localize with the pCLIP contact site reporter.
source: When tagged at the N-terminus, which may interfere with ER targeting, all three proteins co-localize with pCLIP, suggesting that these proteins might play a role at this contact site although we cannot rule out mislocalization due to the tag (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure, including a caveat about potential artifacts.

claim: Csf1 overexpression appears to decrease the number of detectable pCLIP foci and increase the number of LiDER contacts.
source: Csf1 overexpression appears to decrease the number of detectable pCLIP foci and increase the number of LiDER contacts, indicating possible crosstalk between these sites (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the screen with interpretation.

claim: The identification of Hob1, Hob2, and/or Csf1 at several different contacts suggests that these proteins function at multiple localizations.
source: Moreover, the identification of Hob1, Hob2, and/or Csf1 at several different contacts suggests that these proteins, like yeast Vps13 and human VPS13A, VPS13C, and ATG2A (Bean et al., 2018; Kumar et al., 2018; Tamura et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2019; Yeshaw et al., 2019), function at multiple localizations.
evidence: This is an inference from the data with citations to published research on related proteins.

claim: The LiDER reporter co-localized with and/or was affected by 59 proteins.
source: In our screen the LiDER reporter co-localized with and/or was affected by 59 proteins (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of screening results with reference to figure.

claim: Mdm1 was found amongst the hits for the LiDER screen.
source: As expected, we found the known LiDER protein Mdm1 amongst the hits for this screen.
evidence: This is a screening result that validates the approach by identifying a known protein.

claim: Ypr097w both co-localized with and increased the brightness and frequency of the LiDER reporter in cells.
source: Additionally, we identified Ypr097w, a protein of unknown function that both co-localized with and increased the brightness and frequency of the LiDER reporter in cells (Figure 3A, bottom panel).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the screen with reference to figure.

claim: Ypr097w has a Phox homology (PX) domain.
source: Ypr097w has a Phox homology (PX) domain, which is present in Mdm1 and a large number of proteins conserved across all eukaryotic kingdoms, and which interacts with several anionic lipids, including the phosphoinositide species phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) (Chandra et al., 2019; Yu and Lemmon, 2001).
evidence: This is a statement about protein domain structure supported by citations.

claim: Ypr097w contains a predicted FFAT motif.
source: Furthermore, Ypr097w contains a predicted FFAT motif (two phenylalanines, FF, in an acidic tract), a conserved amino acid sequence that enables the interaction of several proteins with the major sperm protein (MSP) domain of VAMP-associated protein (VAP) proteins (Scs2 and Scs22 in yeast) (Slee and Levine, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about protein sequence features supported by citation.

claim: The FFAT motif is present in several contact site proteins where it enables the formation of contact sites between the ER and other organelles.
source: This sequence is present in several contact site proteins, where it enables the formation of contact sites between the ER and other organelles (Murphy and Levine, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: mCherry-Ypr097w under control of a strong promoter localized to internal puncta, several of which co-localize with the LD stain BODIPY on the interface with the ER.
source: To confirm the localization of Ypr097w in the absence of a synthetic reporter we re-tagged it at the N-terminus with mCherry under the control of a strong promoter (Figure 3B) and imaged its location relative to both the ER and LDs. In these conditions, Ypr097w localized to internal puncta, several of which co-localize with the LD stain, BODIPY, on the interface with the ER (Figure 3B), supporting our original observation.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Endogenously tagged Ypr097w showed a different distribution than when overexpressed, being found primarily at buds and bud necks with reduced localization to LDs.
source: When using the endogenous promoter to tag Ypr097w with GFP at either the N- or C-terminus (both tags support the function of the protein, see Figure 5A later in the article), Ypr097w showed a different distribution than when overexpressed – it was found primarily at buds and bud necks, with reduced localization to LDs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figures.

claim: GFP-Ypr097w expressed from the moderate constitutive ADH1 promoter localized to the bud and bud neck with some increase in the number of internal puncta.
source: In this strain, GFP-Ypr097w was more clearly detected and showed a similar distribution pattern to the endogenous promoter, localizing to the bud and bud neck with some increase in the number of internal puncta (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Nearly 60% of cells expressing GFP-Ypr097w from the ADH1 promoter were devoid of a punctate signal and appeared to have a general cytosolic localization.
source: Additionally, many cells (nearly 60%) were devoid of a punctate signal and appeared to have a general cytosolic localization.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments.

claim: GFP-Ypr097w localization was affected by the cell cycle, with a bud/bud neck localization more common in cells with large buds.
source: Interestingly, GFP-Ypr097w localization was also affected by the cell cycle, with a bud/bud neck localization more common in cells with large buds (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Ypr097w accumulates at LDs in Δfld1 mutants.
source: We found that Ypr097w accumulates at LDs in Δfld1 mutants (Figure 3D), corroborating previously published proteomic analysis of these structures (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure and citation to published research.

claim: A genome-wide DHFR protein fragment complementation screen showed that the strongest Ypr097w interactors consist primarily of well-characterized LD-localized enzymes.
source: Second, we performed a genome-wide protein fragment complementation screen based on a split dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) enzyme (Tarassov et al., 2008 Supplementary file 3). This screen, which measures interactions based on colony size after multiple days of growth, showed that the strongest interactors (Z-Score >2.5), which represent proteins in close proximity to Ypr097w, consist primarily of well-characterized LD-localized enzymes (Figure 3E–F)
evidence: This is a result from a genome-wide screen with reference to figures and supplementary file.

claim: The strongest Ypr097w interactors include ER membrane proteins that localize to and help shape regions of tubular ER, such as Rtn1, Yop1, and Sey1.
source: and include ER membrane proteins that localize to, and help shape, regions of tubular ER, such as Rtn1, Yop1, and Sey1 (De Craene et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Voeltz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a result from the DHFR screen with citations to published research on the identified proteins.

claim: Bud neck-localized proteins were not enriched in the DHFR screen.
source: In contrast, bud neck-localized proteins were not enriched in this screen.
evidence: This is a result from the DHFR screen.

claim: GFP-Ypr097w is present in purified LD fractions.
source: Finally, we biochemically purified LDs from cells expressing GFP-Ypr097w under control of the moderate constitutive ADH1 promoter and found that GFP-Ypr097w is indeed present in purified LD fractions (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a direct result from biochemical fractionation experiments with reference to figure.

claim: When cells were shifted from nutrient-containing media to PBS, both endogenous and ADH1pr-expressed GFP-Ypr097w rapidly (<2 min) re-localized from bud/bud neck to the cytosol.
source: Indeed, we found that when cells were shifted from nutrient-containing media to phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), both endogenous (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) and ADH1pr-expressed (not shown), GFP-Ypr097w rapidly (<2 min) re-localized from bud/bud neck to the cytosol, an effect that was blocked if the PBS was supplemented with glucose.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Longer glucose starvation in synthetic media led to a mostly cytosolic localization of Ypr097w.
source: Similarly, longer glucose starvation in synthetic media led to a mostly cytosolic localization of this protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: In stationary cells, GFP-Ypr097w localized mostly in a punctate pattern.
source: In contrast, in stationary cells, GFP-Ypr097w localized mostly in a punctate pattern (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F, left panel)
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Upon replenishment with fresh media, GFP-Ypr097w quickly shifted to a mix of punctate and bud/bud neck localization.
source: which quickly shifted to a mix of punctate and bud/bud neck upon replenishment with fresh media (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F, right panel).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Several phosphorylation sites have been identified in Ypr097w in high throughput studies, including phosphorylation of residue S451 in the region flanking the predicted FFAT motif.
source: In fact, several phosphorylation sites have been identified in Ypr097w in high throughput studies (Beltrao et al., 2012; Lanz et al., 2021), including phosphorylation of residue S451 in the region flanking the predicted FFAT motif (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: Supported by citations to published research with reference to figure.

claim: The punctate localization of Ypr097w increased in cells lacking both yeast VAP proteins (∆scs2/∆scs22).
source: Moreover, the punctate localization of Ypr097w increased in cells lacking both yeast VAP proteins (∆scs2/∆scs22) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Expression of phosphomimetic (S451E; S451D) or phospho-null (S451A) mutants, or a mutant lacking the FFAT motif (Y456A, D458A), did not show any clear differences in localization relative to wild type Ypr097w.
source: However, we found that expression of either phosphomimetic (S451E; S451D) or phospho-null (S451A) mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), or a mutant lacking the FFAT motif (Y456A, D458A; data not shown), in a strain lacking endogenous Ypr097w, did not show any clear differences in localization relative to the wild type (WT) Ypr097w control.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Neither phosphorylation of S451 nor the presence of the FFAT motif regulates Ypr097w targeting under regular growth conditions.
source: This suggests that neither phosphorylation of S451 nor the presence of the FFAT motif regulates YPR097w targeting under regular growth conditions.
evidence: This is an inference from the mutant localization data.

claim: Truncations that perturb either the N or C-termini of Ypr097w disrupt protein localization.
source: By testing a series of protein fragments, we found that truncations that perturb either the N or C-termini disrupt protein localization, and we did not identify any domain that was sufficient for localization to either LDs or to the bud/bud neck (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a direct result from testing protein truncations with reference to figure.

claim: Structural homology modeling by HHpred showed that the unnamed regions bracketing DUF3818 in Ypr097w have similar levels of conservation as the named domains.
source: Structural homology modeling by HHpred (Gabler et al., 2020) showed that the unnamed regions bracketing DUF3818 (Figure 4A) have similar levels of conservation as the named domains
evidence: This is a result from bioinformatic analysis with reference to figure.

claim: All regions of Ypr097w except the PX domain are made up of multiple alpha-helices.
source: and that all regions, except the PX domain (which is longer than previously noted) are made up of multiple alpha-helices (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result from structural analysis.

claim: Full-length Ypr097w functions as a single unit.
source: Together with our truncation results, this suggests that full-length Ypr097w functions as a single unit.
evidence: This is an inference from truncation and structural data.

claim: Ypr097w forms a previously undocumented fold.
source: However, other than the PX domain, HHpred searches did not find any homology to solved structures or remote homology to other proteins. This implies that Ypr097w forms a previously undocumented fold.
evidence: This is an inference from the lack of homology to known structures.

claim: AlphaFold2 structure prediction for Ypr097w shows that the different all-helical regions interact in cis to form a sphere ~7 nm in diameter.
source: AlphaFold2 outputs for Ypr097w and its full-length homologs in both C. albicans and S. pombe all predict that the different all-helical regions, which appear separate in the one-dimensional map (Figure 4A), interact in cis to form a sphere ~7 nm in diameter (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: The N-terminal PXB domain of Ypr097w folds intimately together with the unnamed C-terminal region.
source: In particular, the N-terminal PXB domain folds intimately together with the unnamed C-terminal region (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: The PX domain of Ypr097w is oriented to expose its PI3P binding site, which would allow Ypr097w to dock onto membranes.
source: The PX domain is oriented to expose its PI3P binding site, which would allow Ypr097w to dock onto membranes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference from the structural model with reference to figure.

claim: Among five AlphaFold2 models of Ypr097w homologs, the PX-negative S. pombe homolog is the most confidently predicted.
source: Among the five AlphaFold2 models, the PX-negative S. pombe homolog is the most confidently predicted (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), implying that the PX domain is unnecessary for the overall fold.
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 predictions with inference about domain importance, with reference to figure.

claim: The predicted Ypr097w sphere is hollow with an internal cavity.
source: A striking feature of the predicted Ypr097w sphere is that it is hollow with an internal cavity (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: The surface of the cavity in Ypr097w is mainly hydrophobic (lipophilic).
source: The surface of the cavity is mainly hydrophobic (lipophilic) (Figure 4C), a feature that is highly conserved (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of the AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: Multiple tunnels potentially provide access from the cytosol to the internal cavity of Ypr097w.
source: Multiple tunnels potentially provide access from the cytosol (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-E, arrows).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of the AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figure.

claim: The internal cavity of Ypr097w has a volume of 29 nm3, equivalent to a sphere diameter of 3.8 nm.
source: We calculated the internal cavity without the loop and found that it has a volume of 29 nm3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), equivalent to a sphere diameter of 3.8 nm.
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the structural model with reference to figure.

claim: Mutating the hydrophobic residues in the binding pocket of Ypr097w altered the capacity of Ypr097w to localize to LDs and its functionality.
source: Mutating the hydrophobic residues in the binding pocket altered the capacity of Ypr097w to localize to LDs, as well as its functionality (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-D), suggesting the importance of the hydrophobic pocket for structural stability.
evidence: This is a direct result from mutational analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The cavity in Ypr097w resembles those in the family of large lipid transfer proteins related to vitellogenin, including apolipoprotein B.
source: While this α-helical structure is unique, the cavity resembles those in the family of large lipid transfer proteins (LTPs) related to vitellogenin, including apolipoprotein B (Smolenaars et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparison to known protein structures with citation.

claim: In vitellogenin-related proteins, similar sized cavities lined by β-sheets function in passing lipids from membrane sources to diverse destinations.
source: In these proteins, similar sized cavities lined by β-sheets function in passing lipids from membrane sources to diverse destinations.
evidence: This is a statement about known protein function.

claim: AlphaFold2 analysis of Mdm1 revealed that the PXA and nexin-C domains fold together to form a large spherical domain with an interior hydrophobic surface.
source: Strikingly, AlphaFold2 analysis of these proteins revealed that the PXA and nexin-C domains in Mdm1 and Nvj3 fold together to form a large spherical domain with an interior hydrophobic surface (Figure 4E and G) that is highly conserved (Figure 4F and H).
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: AlphaFold2 analysis of Nvj3 revealed that the PXA and nexin-C domains fold together to form a large spherical domain with an interior hydrophobic surface.
source: Strikingly, AlphaFold2 analysis of these proteins revealed that the PXA and nexin-C domains in Mdm1 and Nvj3 fold together to form a large spherical domain with an interior hydrophobic surface (Figure 4E and G) that is highly conserved (Figure 4F and H).
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: The PXA/nexin-C domains in Mdm1 and Nvj3 share no detectable sequence homology to Ypr097w.
source: While the PXA/nexin-C domains share no detectable sequence homology to Ypr097w, the structural similarities suggest that these proteins may share a function that we hypothesize may be in lipid storage or transfer.
evidence: This is a statement about sequence analysis with speculation about function.

claim: No clear changes in the number of LDs were observed in WT, Δypr097w and overexpressed YPR097W cells.
source: To test this, we first looked at the number of LDs in WT, Δypr097w and overexpressed YPR097W (under control of the TDH3pr) cells using the LD marker BODIPY. However, we observed no clear changes in the number of LDs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) or LD morphology (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) in the tested conditions.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figures.

claim: No clear changes in the levels of DAG, TAG, ergosterol, or sterol esters were observed in WT, Δypr097w and TDH3pr-YPR097W cells during mid-logarithmic growth, stationary cultures, and following growth resumption.
source: To test for changes in the total levels of storage lipids, we performed thin layer chromatography (TLC) of WT, Δypr097w and TDH3pr-YPR097W during mid-logarithmic growth, in stationary cultures (24 hr and 48 hr), and following growth resumption during new media replenishment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C). When compared to control cells, no clear changes in the levels of diacylglycerol (DAG), triacylglycerol (TAG), ergosterol (Erg), or sterol esters (SE) were observed in any of the conditions tested.
evidence: This is a direct result from TLC analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Lipidomic analysis of the YPR097W overexpression strain relative to a control strain did not uncover any major global lipid differences.
source: Additionally, lipidomic analysis of the overexpression strain relative to a control strain also did not uncover any major global lipid differences (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct result from lipidomic analysis with reference to figure and supplementary file.

claim: Loss of Ypr097w sensitized cells to Amphotericin B (AmB).
source: Surprisingly, despite the lack of changes in overall ergosterol or SE levels observed by TLC and lipidomics, loss of Ypr097w sensitized cells to AmB (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct result from growth assays with reference to figure.

claim: Treatment with AmB for 90 minutes resulted in a redistribution of Ypr097w, with the protein almost exclusively localizing to LDs.
source: To assay this, we tracked the localization of GFP-Ypr097w in cells treated with AmB for 90 minutes and found that indeed, this resulted in a redistribution of Ypr097w (Figure 5B). Under these conditions, Ypr097w almost exclusively localized to LDs (as marked by Faa4-mCherry).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Fluconazole treatment strongly reduced the level of cellular ergosterol, as shown by the loss of binding of mCherry-D4H to the plasma membrane.
source: As expected, fluconazole treatment strongly reduced the level of cellular ergosterol, as shown by the loss of binding of mCherry-D4H to the plasma membrane (cytosolic signal) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A lower right panels).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Fluconazole treatment led to an increase in the number of cells with bud/bud neck localization for GFP-Ypr097w.
source: In these conditions, where internal ergosterol is also depleted, we actually see an increase in the number of cells with bud/ bud neck localization for GFP-Ypr097w (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: In WT cells, the mCherry-D4H sterol reporter is mostly localized to the PM, with an enhanced signal at the daughter cell.
source: In WT cells, this sterol reporter is mostly localized to the PM, with an enhanced signal at the daughter cell (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: In the absence of Ypr097w, a stronger localization of mCherry-D4H to daughter cells was observed, with additional accumulation of signal at the bud neck.
source: In the absence of Ypr097w, a stronger localization to daughter cells was observed, with the additional accumulation of signal at the bud neck, a phenotype that is mostly absent from WT cells in the conditions tested (Figure 5C, D, (III)).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figures.

claim: In cells where YPR097W is strongly overexpressed under the TDH3 promoter, the distribution of mCherry-D4H was less polarized, with many cells displaying a similar signal between mother and daughter cells.
source: In cells where YPR097W is strongly overexpressed under the TDH3 promoter, the distribution of mCherry-D4H was less polarized, with many cells displaying a similar signal between mother and daughter cells.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments.

claim: Cells overexpressing YPR097W showed a much stronger punctate or mixed pattern of mCherry-D4H than both WT and Δypr097w.
source: Additionally, these cells showed a much stronger punctate or mixed pattern than both WT and Δypr097w, suggesting that overexpression of this protein affects the distribution of accessible ergosterol.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with interpretation.

claim: When both Osh6 and Osh7 are deleted, changes in the distribution of both mCherry-D4H and Ypr097w are observed.
source: Indeed, when we actively decrease the levels of PS on the PM by deleting both Osh6 and Osh7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A; Maeda et al., 2013) we do see changes in the distribution of both mCherry-D4H and Ypr097w.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure and citation.

claim: Deletion or overexpression of YPR097W does not affect the distribution of PS at the plasma membrane.
source: Taking advantage of the PS probe GFP-Lact-C2, we showed that deletion or overexpression of YPR097W does not affect the distribution of PS at the plasma membrane (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B-C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with reference to figure.

claim: Cells overexpressing YPR097W show no significant differences in the total amount of PS.
source: In addition, cells overexpressing YPR097W show no significant differences in the total amount of PS (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D), even compared at the level of PS species (Figure 5—figure supplement 3E), acyl chain saturation (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F), or acyl chain length (Figure 5—figure supplement 3G).
evidence: This is a direct result from lipidomic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Ypr097w appears to play a significant role in ergosterol accessibility, membrane bilayer organization, or localization in the cell.
source: Thus, while Ypr097w does not appear to regulate total ergosterol and sterol ester levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C-D), it appears to play a significant role in ergosterol accessibility, membrane bilayer organization, or localization in the cell.
evidence: This is an inference from the combined data on ergosterol distribution and AmB sensitivity.

claim: The screens identified over 100 new potential contact site residents and effectors in yeast.
source: By scoring both co-localization events and effects on reporter size and abundance, we discovered over 100 new potential contact site residents and effectors in yeast.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the screening results.

claim: Fmp27, Ypr117w (now renamed Hob1 and Hob2), and Csf1 are three homologs of Vps13 and Atg2 that are residents of multiple contact sites.
source: Focusing on several of the newly identified residents, we identified three homologs of Vps13 and Atg2 that are residents of multiple contact sites.
evidence: This is a summary statement of findings from the screen and subsequent analysis.

claim: Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 share their lipid transport domain with Vps13 and Atg2, thus expanding this family of lipid transporters.
source: These proteins share their lipid transport domain, thus expanding this family of lipid transporters.
evidence: This is an inference from structural analysis.

claim: Ypr097w, now called Lec1 (Lipid-droplet Ergosterol Cortex 1), dynamically shifts between lipid droplets and the cell cortex.
source: Analysis of another candidate, Ypr097w, which we now call Lec1 (Lipid-droplet Ergosterol Cortex 1), revealed that this previously uncharacterized protein dynamically shifts between lipid droplets and the cell cortex
evidence: This is a summary statement of findings from imaging experiments.

claim: Lec1 plays a role in regulation of ergosterol distribution in the cell.
source: and plays a role in regulation of ergosterol distribution in the cell.
evidence: This is a summary statement of findings from ergosterol distribution experiments.

claim: The screens were far from being saturating since only ~1/3 of yeast proteins were screened.
source: Of note is that our screens were far from being saturating since we only screened ~1/3 of yeast proteins, albeit those with the highest chance of being direct residents and effectors.
evidence: This is a statement about the scope and limitations of the screen.

claim: Previously known contact site proteins were detected at the NVJ (Nvj1, Mdm1, Nvj3, and Lam6), at the LiDER (Mdm1), and at the PerMit (Pex34 and Fzo1).
source: As a clear example of the effectiveness of this technique, we have detected previously known contact site proteins at the NVJ (Nvj1, Mdm1, Nvj3, and Lam6), at the LiDER (Mdm1), and at the PerMit (Pex34 and Fzo1).
evidence: This is a summary statement of screening results that validates the approach.

claim: Hob1, Hob2, and Csf1 may localize to multiple contact sites like yeast Vps13 and human VPS13A, VPS13C, and ATG2A.
source: Moreover, the identification of Hob1, Hob2, and/or Csf1 at several different contacts suggests that these proteins, like yeast Vps13 and human VPS13A, VPS13C, and ATG2A (Bean et al., 2018; Kumar et al., 2018; Tamura et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2019; Yeshaw et al., 2019), function at multiple localizations.
evidence: This is an inference from the screening data with citations to published research on related proteins.

claim: Csf1 was recently shown to function in lipid homeostasis under cold stress and in cells with rewired glycerophospholipid synthesis pathways.
source: Furthermore, Csf1 was recently shown to function in lipid homeostasis under cold stress and in cells with rewired glycerophospholipid synthesis pathways (John Peter et al., 2022)
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: Csf1 has been implicated in the transport of phosphatidylethanolamine from other organelles to the ER.
source: and has been implicated in the transport of phosphatidylethanolamine from other organelles to the ER (Toulmay et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: Hob1/2 and Csf1 have homologs in mammalian cells – BLTP2 (also known as KIAA0100/BCOX1) for Hob1/2, and BLTP1 (also known as KIAA1109) for Csf1.
source: Additionally, these proteins have homologs in mammalian cells – BLTP2 (for Bridge-like Lipid Transfer Protein family member 2) (also known as KIAA0100/BCOX1) for Hob1/2, and BLTP1 (also known as KIAA1109) for Csf1.
evidence: This is a statement about protein homology.

claim: BLTP1 and BLTP2 have been implicated in human disease.
source: Both of these have been implicated in human disease (Gueneau et al., 2018; Kane et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2014; Song et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: Lec1 has a PX domain for binding lipid headgroups and one of the strongest FFAT motifs in yeast.
source: This protein stood out as it has a PX domain for binding lipid headgroups, as well as one of the strongest FFAT motifs in yeast (Loewen et al., 2003; Slee and Levine, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about protein domain structure supported by citations.

claim: Lec1 appears to act as a sensor of nutrient status, changing its cellular localization under multiple metabolic conditions.
source: However, we determined that Lec1 appears to act as a sensor of nutrient status, changing its cellular localization under multiple metabolic conditions, highlighting the ability of our screen to identify even transient contact site residents.
evidence: This is an inference from the localization data under different conditions.

claim: The N- and C-terminal regions of Lec1 are highly interwoven.
source: The N- and C-terminal regions of the protein are highly interwoven, which may explain how N- and C-terminal truncations disrupt its localization.
evidence: This is a result from structural prediction with inference about truncation effects.

claim: The predicted structure of Lec1 shows a large internal hydrophobic cavity with multiple channels opening to the cytosol.
source: Strikingly, the predicted structure of this protein shows a large internal hydrophobic cavity, with multiple channels opening to the cytosol.
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction.

claim: The hydrophobicity of the residues lining the pocket in Lec1 is highly conserved and functionally important.
source: The hydrophobicity of the residues lining the pocket is highly conserved and functionally important.
evidence: This is a result from structural analysis and mutational experiments.

claim: Lec1 could potentially accommodate a mixture of many different neutral lipids and amphipathic lipids.
source: Hence, we hypothesize that Lec1 could potentially accommodate a mixture of many different neutral lipids (e.g. triolein 1.62 nm3) and amphipathic lipids (e.g. DOPC 1.3 nm3).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the calculated cavity volume.

claim: Mdm1 and Nvj3 fold together to form large spherical domains with an interior hydrophobic surface that is highly conserved.
source: We found two additional proteins that share this predicted form (using AlphaFold2) - Mdm1 and Nvj3, which fold together to form large spherical domains with an interior hydrophobic surface (Figure 4E and G) that is highly conserved (Figure 4F and H).
evidence: This is a result from AlphaFold2 structural prediction with reference to figures.

claim: Δlec1 cells are sensitive to AmB, an antifungal drug that interacts with free ergosterol at the PM.
source: We found that Δlec1 cells are sensitive to AmB, an antifungal drug that interacts with free ergosterol at the PM and is suggested to induce membrane permeabilization and ergosterol removal (Anderson et al., 2014; Gray et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct result from growth assays with citations to published research on AmB mechanism.

claim: Sensitivity to AmB has been observed for other contact site proteins, such as Lam1 (Ysp1), Lam2 (Ysp2) and Lam3 (Sip3), which localize to ER-PM contact sites and are involved in the retrograde transport of ergosterol from the PM to the ER.
source: Sensitivity to AmB has also been observed for other contact site proteins, such as Lam1 (Ysp1), Lam2 (Ysp2) and Lam3 (Sip3), which localize to ER-PM contact sites and are involved in the retrograde transport of ergosterol from the PM to the ER (Gatta et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research.

claim: Changes in the levels of Lec1 affect the localization of free ergosterol in the cell, affecting its distribution between mother and daughter cells as well as internal reservoirs.
source: By taking advantage of an ergosterol-binding fluorescent probe, we show that changes in the levels of Lec1 affect the localization of free ergosterol in the cell, affecting its distribution between mother and daughter cells as well as internal reservoirs.
evidence: This is a direct result from imaging experiments using the mCherry-D4H probe.

claim: The stronger accumulation of accessible ergosterol at the bud and bud neck of cells lacking Lec1 could explain how these mutants are more sensitive to AmB.
source: The stronger accumulation of accessible ergosterol at the bud and bud neck of cells lacking Lec1 could explain how these mutants are more sensitive to AmB, as higher levels of accessible ergosterol would make budding cells more sensitive to this drug.
evidence: This is an inference from the combined data on ergosterol distribution and AmB sensitivity.

claim: Lec1 plays a role in the transbilayer organization or mobilization of ergosterol between membranes in yeast.
source: Together with the lack of changes in overall ergosterol levels in these cells, our results suggest that Lec1 plays a role in the transbilayer organization or mobilization of ergosterol between membranes in yeast.
evidence: This is an inference from the combined data on ergosterol levels and distribution.

claim: Upon addition of AmB that binds accessible ergosterol, Lec1 shifts from buds and bud necks to LDs where it may either sequester or mobilize sterols.
source: Consistent with this, upon addition of AmB that binds accessible ergosterol, Lec1 shifts from buds and bud necks to LDs where it may either sequester or mobilize sterols.
evidence: This is a direct observation from imaging experiments with speculation about function.

claim: Despite the large volume of work on contact sites, multiple contact residents and regulators still await exploration.
source: More generally our results show that despite the large volume of work on contact sites, multiple contact residents and regulators still await exploration.
evidence: This is a general conclusion from the screening results.
